Synopsis:
A Reuters/Nikkei Research survey of 224 Japanese firms shows ~68% support PM Takaichi's economic policies, particularly her pro-investment growth strategy targeting AI, semiconductors, and strategic industries (¥370T public/private investment through FY2040). The most contested measure is a proposed food sales tax cut to 1% from 8%, which critics warn would inflate the national debt and weaken the yen. 46% of firms want Takaichi to serve beyond her current LDP term (ending Sept 2027). On FX, most firms prefer USD/JPY in the 150-160 range. The BoJ is widely expected to hike rates to 1.25% at its Sept 17-18 meeting, with the yen already firming on that expectation (~153.58).
